events.description: Igorrr, the French avant-garde project masterminded by Gautier Serre, brings their North American Tour 2026 to the Roxian Theatre in Pittsburgh, PA on September 21, 2026. Known for their genre-defying blend of baroque, death metal, breakcore, and classical music, Igorrr delivers one of the most unique live experiences in heavy music. Joining them as special guests are Secret Chiefs 3, the eclectic experimental ensemble led by Trey Spruance known for blending surf, metal, Middle Eastern, and sacred music traditions, and VMO (Violent Magic Orchestra), the Japanese experimental noise/industrial project. This event is presented by Citizens. Igorrr on Bandcamp: https://igorrr.bandcamp.com/ Secret Chiefs 3 on Bandcamp: https://secretchiefs3.bandcamp.com/

Anika, the German-British vocalist known for her deadpan delivery and work with Beak> producer Geoff Barrow, brings her own brand of hypnotic post-punk and dub-inflected electronic music to open the night. Presented by Opus One Concerts with support from 91.3 WYEP. Tickets and event details available at www.nationoflanguage.com/events.

events.title: Sound Series: L'Rain
events.description:
We welcome L’Rain, the musical project of multi-instrumentalist, composer, producer and curator Taja Cheek. Operating at the intersections of art, music, film, fashion and cultural discourse, Cheek’s sensibility, crafted in collaboration with Ben Chapoteau-Katz and Andrew Lappin, transcends disciplines, blurs traditional genre boundaries and deconstructs pop tropes. The 2021 album Fatigue garnered critical acclaim including album of the year from The Wire, and in May 2026, L’Rain recorded a live album and concert film at Walker Art Center in Minneapolis. Cheek was guest curator of the 2024 Whitney Biennial and currently is the artistic director of Performance Space New York.

Doors open at 7:30 p.m.
This performance is primarily standing room only. Limited seating is available upon advance request. We are committed to offering inclusive, engaging experiences for people of all abilities. To request accommodations to enhance your visit, please contact access@warhol.org or call 412.237.8354.
L’Rain has partnered with PLUS1 so that $1 from every ticket sold goes to Sounds of Saving and their work designing and providing tools, content, resources and curriculum to young people on how to discover and utilize music to support their mental health and wellness.

Co-presented with 91.3 WYEP Presents

https://lrain.bandcamp.com/

events.title: Weaving: Directed Open Studio with Margaret Dugger
events.description: Expand your weaving skills with the guidance of weaver Margaret Dugger in this self-directed small group offering! Weaving: Directed Open Studio with Margaret Dugger Fall Term, 3-Month Loom Rental with Weaving Seminar Meetings Dates: September 23 – December 23 Seminar Session Meeting Dates: Wednesdays: September 23, October 7, October 21, November 4, November 18, December 2, December 16 Times of seminar sessions: 6pm-9pm Description: Expand your weaving skills, and weave in community this fall! This offering is part loom rental, part in-depth weaving seminar! Weavers will design and weave individualized projects on one of Contemporary Craft’s looms. Throughout the fall, weavers in the Directoed Open Studio will have access to their looms during CC’s open studio hours + many Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday evenings. Plus! Margaret will offer 7 three-hour seminar sessions in which participants will have the opportunity to dive deeper into specifics of their chosen project, including reading—or adapting—a weaving pattern draft, selecting yarn, measuring and estimating material needs, and finishing techniques. These seminar sessions will be spaced out so that weavers have the chance to practice working independently in between sessions, while also feeling supported knowing that when they arrive at their next question, another seminar session is coming up soon! This offering is for weavers with some experience but who might need a little assistance in designing and figuring out how to make the cloth of their dreams! Ideally, weavers will have completed Weaving 1 at CC or who have some other experience with weaving. A variety of loom widths are available. When you register, someone from the studio will reach out to find out more about which loom might be the best fit for you and your project! Tuition: $450 (does not include materials) Materials: Weavers provide their own material. Some yarns are available for purchase from the studio. Registration: Register through Eventbrite. If you are viewing this listing via the Contemporary Craft website on your phone, click this link to visit the Eventbrite registration page. Scholarships: Note: We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are often available—with some limitations— to offset some of the financial burden of attending a class. Fill out the scholarship form here. You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Fibers Program Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Location: Contemporary Craft, TImmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the second floor. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded through Eventbrite, or you may leave your workshop fee in your Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist Margaret Dugger is an artist currently based in Pittsburgh, PA. Originally trained as an artisan handweaver, she now creates weavings that reflect on the quiet moments of our daily lives. Using the processes of addition, removal, and transformation, Margaret explores concepts of interconnection, the sacred within the mundane, and historical practices brought into the contemporary. She engages with the ancient traditions of textile work and art making, using cloth and thread as her medium.Since pursuing her bachelor’s degree at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago, her work has branched out into new mediums including paper, sculpture, and book arts. Weavers having fun tying up treadles on the loom! A view of looms in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft! Come weave with us!

events.title: Screenwriting: Discovering Your Premise workshop
events.description:
Get to the heart of your screenplay idea and leave with a strong logline in just one night.

This one-night intensive workshop, led by Thiel College professor Matthew Humphrey, will assist both aspiring and emerging screenwriters in getting to the very core of their story. Through targeted discussions, practical exercises, and workshopping with peers, you will learn how to identify and succinctly describe the essential elements of a screenplay.

Taking the next step, you will learn how to shape those elements into a compelling, pitch-ready logline.  Whether you are starting a fresh draft or refining an existing screenplay, you will walk away with more clarity on your narrative and a compelling pitch for your film. 

Participants are encouraged to arrive with at least a basic idea for a screenplay. Bringing a laptop is encouraged but not required.

events.description: SPARTA with support from PUBLIC OPINION $20 ADV / $25 DOS / $85 VIP 7PM DOORS / 8PM MUSIC ALL AGES VIP PACKAGE INCLUDES: - One general admission ticket - Early entry into the venue - Exclusive meet and greet with Sparta - Personal photograph with Sparta - Intimate Q&A with Sparta - Solo Jim song - Limited edition silkscreen tour poster, autographed by Sparta - Official meet & greet laminate and lanyard - Priority merchandise shopping - Limited availability for fans of... At The Drive-In, Cursive, Thursday BIO: It all started with John Candy. Some 31 years after the comedian’s death, Jim Ward was watching a documentary about him, and in it Macaulay Culkin—who had starred in a number of films with the late actor—said something that really stuck with the musician. So much so, in fact, that, after months of pondering and overthinking what Sparta’s sixth full-length album would be named, Ward decided that those very words—“cut a silhouette”—should be the title. “He said that when he met John Candy, he just entered your brain and cut a silhouette,” says Ward. “Like, he just left an impression is the way I see it. And when I heard him say that, I was like ‘Oh! That’s what I want this record to be.’ I want it to leave an impression. At this point in my career, that's what I yearn for. I'm working so hard to make something meaningful to me, and I really want people to get a chance to feel it as well.” Of course, Ward’s 30-plus year career in music has already cut plenty of silhouettes, first as a vital member of pioneering post-hardcore outfit At The Drive-In, then as the frontman of Sparta. The latter released their first album, Wiretap Scars, in 2002, second record Porcelain in 2004, and third LP, Threes, in 2006. Due to a couple of hiatuses, a fourth album, Trust The River, didn’t arrive until 2020, followed two years later by a self-titled fifth album. But there have also been a handful of solo releases, a collaborative album with poet Bobby Byrd, and an LP and an EP by Sleepercar, Ward’s alternative country project, not to mention successful anniversary tours celebrating those first two Sparta albums. It all adds up to a legacy—and yes, that’s the correct word to use—that has been leaving an indelible impression on people for a long time now. “I'm humbled by that,” he says, “and appreciative of it. I don't dismiss it at all. I spend a lot of time listening to people tell me how important the music I’ve been a part of making is to them, and it's not lost on me, but it's also not about me in that moment. So I'm more than aware of it. I've been living it for a really long time and I’m really fucking grateful for it.” Though it doesn’t necessarily move Ward in the here and now—the past, after all, is the past— it nevertheless still has an impact on the present, and the music he makes in it. “Some of what comes through all that,” he continues, “is the question of am I ever going to do this again? Do I want to do this again? Do I have anything to add to anything? Is anything I want to say important enough for anyone to give a fuck about? That's why that phrase hit me so hard. Because when you come out the other side, you’re like ‘Oh, this is something I believe in, and that I think will leave an impression.’” He isn’t exaggerating. Produced, engineered and recorded in seven days at the Magpie Cage Recording Studio by the iconic J. Robbins—“When I was 15, he was the center of my musical world,” beams Ward, “so who better for me to want to impress than my literal hero?”—Cut A Silhouette begins with the frantic, impassioned rush of “Split Lip” before charging into the urgent insistence of “Crater”. The latter song, along with “Mouthbreather”, which immediately follows it, were both written with Frank Iero, though the My Chemical Romance guitarist doesn’t play on them. “See You Soon”, a gorgeous, lilting explosion of slow-motion power-pop, was co-written with Kemble Walters (Chevelle, Juliette And The Licks). He does play on that song, as does Adrian Borgeois, who adds some tender piano to the melancholy equation. J. Robbins also features on a number of the songs, as does Brooks Harlan, who plays in Jawbox with Robbins, as well as in War On Women, while Carlos Arévalo from Chicano Batman plays guitar on the hopeful fragility of “Midnights”. Really, though, this is pure, unadulterated Sparta. These days completed by bassist Matt Miller and drummer Neil Hennessey, the band have made a record that’s a culmination of the perfectly imperfect chemistry that flows between the three of them. Cut A Silhouette, then, is a collision of past and present. It builds off Sparta’s legacy, but equally continues the evolution of a band that has never rested on its laurels. The only thing on this record that shines as much as that chemistry between the trio is the community spirit that helped create it. Recorded in just seven days, Ward felt himself traveling back in time in the studio, yet also—as ever—forging forwards while doing so. “It feels like a return to the community I came from and I love,” says Wars. “All the early At The Drive-In stuff was done in no more than a week until Relationship Of Command. Then Sparta sort of existed in this world of major labels and million dollar budgets and craziness. It's so easy to look at that now and say I don't belong there, but at the time I was trying really hard. When I go back and look at photos, though, to me it always looks like I'm wearing somebody else's clothes. It doesn't seem natural. So when Equal Vision asked me 'Why do you want to come here?' I said, 'I just want to come home.' They represent a community that I feel comfortable in—people that are doing it for the same reason that I do it.” While you might expect that last self-titled previous full-length to have been the one to bring Sparta home—after all, self-titled records are often made with that intention—that’s actually the role Ward has given Cut A Silhouette. But he admits that the previous record—one he says felt like it was made from disparate parts being brought together—was a necessary process to go through for this one to exist. “This feels like we're a fucking band again,” he says. “All three of us are in a room, we're all writing together, we're listening to each other—this is now a constructive creative process, and it's now the end of this era. Like, I made it through.” That’s a sentiment summed up by album finale “Glimmer”. A gorgeous, redemptive anthem, it’s a soul-searching dose of optimism and intention, a new beginning blossoming from the dust of what once was. And while that still remains—and will forever—Cut A Silhouette aims to leave an ever greater impression from this point on. “Before this time period,” continues Ward, “I was struggling in a lot of ways, like a lot of people were coming out of COVID. But it was also being in the midpart of your career, when you're at the beginning of being washed up or old or seeing gray hair and wrinkles, when you feel out of date and irrelevant. I was just like, ‘What the fuck am I doing with my life?' We'd done tours celebrating the anniversaries of Wiretap Scars and Porcelain, but I don't want to live on that nostalgia. I don't feel comfortable in my own skin. So whether I did it on purpose or not, with this album I think I sabotaged my way to freedom.”

events.title: Intro to Forging Series with Danielle Brannigan
events.description: Discover the possibilities of working with ferrous and non-ferrous metals! 6-Week Series Date: Thursdays, September 24th – October 29th Time: 6pm – 9pm, each Thursday Description: Explore the possibilities of forging with copper, brass, and mild steel! Students will experiment with cold working, annealing, fold forming, air chasing, and surface development while learning how different metals respond to heat, force, and forming. Over six weeks, students will create individual projects, refine techniques, and develop the skills necessary to work with metal. Your instructor will provide demonstrations, open studio time, guidance, and feedback throughout the process, concluding with finishing and a group sharing of completed work! Students will learn studio safety, proper tool/equipment use, and walk away with new skills and feeling inspired! Students will leave with foundational skills in forging, forming, and working with copper, brass, and mild steel, along with individual pieces or studies exploring jewelry, sculpture, functional, or mixed-media applications. This class will involve hot metal, fire, and repetitive swinging of a hammer, it can be somewhat physically demanding at times, so slight stamina is recommended. Tuition: $330+ $60 materials fee Materials: All materials will be provided. Students should wear natural fibers such as cotton and denim. Uncuffed pants and closed-toe shoes are required (no shorts or sandals permitted). Long hair should be restrained. Safety glasses and hearing protection are provided; however, participants may bring their own if preferred. We recommend bringing a water bottle to stay hydrated. This workshop is in an open air studio, bring a coat to keep warm before the forges get fired up! Location: Contemporary Craft – Timmons Studios, Blacksmithing Studio (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201) Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded through Eventbrite, or you may leave your workshop fee in your Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. ANY WORKSHOP OR INDIVIDUAL SESSION CANCELLATIONS WILL BE COMMUNICATED VIA EMAIL. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. We are unable to refund materials cost for this workshop. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist Danielle Brannigan is a Pittsburgh-based silversmith, blacksmith, artist, and educator who works across jewelry, small- and large-scale sculpture, metal fabrication, and welding. She loves working with all forms of metal, with a particular affinity for steel and copper. Her practice is rooted in experimentation, hands-on making, and discovering new possibilities within the material. She has a special interest in reclaimed steel and recycled materials, giving new life to materials through transformation and reuse. In her current explorations, Danielle is experimenting with enameling steel, exploring the interplay of color, surface, texture, and form. As an educator, she encourages curiosity, experimentation, and a willingness to push the material in unexpected directions.

events.title: 2026 Backyard Docs Film Festival
events.description:
Backyard Docs Film Festival is an annual celebration of non-fiction cinema that explores our region’s Rust Belt and Appalachian identity.
The festival showcases documentary films and filmmakers directly connected to our region or that share our region’s identity and culture. Formerly known as The Rust Belt & Appalachia Documentary Film Festival, the Backyard Docs Film Festival continues its trademark DIY screening style, holding screenings in unconventional locations such as abandoned factories, dive bars, rooftops, and backyards. The four-day event will also feature a panel discussion with regional industry leaders in documentary and visual journalism, private rough-cut feedback sessions, professional development workshops with world-renowned filmmakers, and, of course, great afterparties. It’s the one time of year when filmmakers, journalists, and artists of all stripes can come together, build new connections, and help redefine the story of the Rust Belt and Appalachia.

events.title: Joey Adams w/ Trey Johnston & Noah Collins
events.description: Doors 7pm | Show 8pm$12 ADV | $15 DOS21+Joey Adams - An Ohio native moved to West Virginia, Joey Adams combines both the rock n roll he grew up on with the Appalachian bluegrass hes come to love. Through the use of his sharp storytelling abilities, Adams crafts the lyrics of his songs to talk about his own experiences as well as others. From writing intense break up songs like Deep End to laid back ballads about home such as East Ohio, Adams continues to write relatable and meaningful songs.Trey Johnston - Born and raised in the outskirts of rural Ohio, Southern Rock and Country music have major influences on Treys songwriting style as well as musical accompaniment preferences. With a more modern twist on Southern Rock or Grunge Country music. Noah Collins - A Chattanooga native, Noah Collins lived in the Dominican Republic for twenty-four months. It was there in the campos where Collins says he developed his percussive finger picking style. 2007 brought him back home to begin work on his debut release Heart on a Line. Americana-UK gave the album 7 of 10 stars after its release in 2008.With coarse, heart-filled vocals comparable to Manchester-born musician David Gray and American songwriter Bob Dylan, Noah Collins delivers a moving performance. A compositional minimalist, Collins compliments simple words with discreet rhythms.

Pure effing fire, trust that 🧨

Hosted by the booth bunnies @asajeanz, @gee.bee.412, @sarahquiana, & @terrez_000 🐰

events.title: Introduction to Improv Embroidery with Alison Stein
events.description: Create an improvisational embroidery piece, taking a "doodle approach" to stitches! 3-Hour Workshop Date: Saturday, September 26 Time: 2 – 5 pm Description: This workshop will provide gentle encouragement and instruction on how to create beautiful embroidery pieces using an unplanned, improvisational approach. Whether you have never picked up a needle or are an experienced embroiderer, this method is available to you. Enjoy the beauty of color, textile and fiber without any stress of “messing up,” which is simply impossible in this approach! Techniques and Skills covered in this class will include: Learning (or unlearning) the mindset of embroidery without a pattern. Sourcing, selecting and preparing fabric and fiber for improv embroidery. Taking a “doodle approach” to embroidery stitches. We will take a different approach to learning or re-learning the basic embroidery stitches, encouraging beginners to feel confident, and more advanced students will have a new way of thinking about and building on stitches they already know. Thinking about color choices and composition Methods for addressing results you don’t love. Tuition: $65 + $15 materials fee Note: We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are available-with some limitations- to offset some of the financial burden of attending a class. Fill out the scholarship application here , and you can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Fibers Program Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Materials: All materials will be provided, however, participants are encouraged to bring any tools that they need to aid in seeing up-close: reading glasses, magnifyers, etc… Location: Contemporary Craft, Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the second floor. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded through Eventbrite, or you may leave your workshop fee in your Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist Alison J. Stein is an artist, teacher and writer based in Carnegie, PA, in the Pittsburgh metro area. She makes vibrant textile art, paintings, prints and book art, and enjoys blurring the boundaries between traditional techniques and contemporary art.

A celebrated alumnus of DePaul University’s renowned Theatre School, Denny first broke through with a standout performance in Hulu’s Looking for Alaska, a critically acclaimed series boasting a 92% Rotten Tomatoes rating. He went on to appear in two seasons of Taylor Sheridan’s hit Paramount+ drama Mayor of Kingstown, further solidifying his dramatic range. Why'd We Book It? In 2026, he takes the stage at Netflix Is a Joke, solidifying his place among the most sought-after rising voices in entertainment. This summer, he joins the Kevin Langue Show as a key performer on an ambitious 18- city national theatre tour, bringing his sharp timing and undeniable charisma to audiences across the country. events.title: Decade Shifter
events.description:
Decade Shifter
Date: September 26, 2026

Time: 9:00 PM – 4:00 AM

Tickets: $20 / $25

Admission: 21+

stress tess (@stress.tess)

stress tess is a Brooklyn-based DJ exploring the hypnotic edges of techno and psychedelic dance music. Her long-form sets move patiently through shimmering minimalism, pulsing rhythms, and deep groove, creating immersive soundscapes that invite listeners inward. She is a founding member of Vortex, the collective behind Area X, a New York party series devoted to cultivating intimate dance floors and expansive states of listening.

dj33L (@dj_33l)


dj33L is a DJ and organizer based in NYC. A product of Brooklyn’s DIY music scene, he seeks to contribute more ways in which we can hold space for each other and advance our shared journey of understanding and self discovery. dj33L is drawn to hypnotic and minimal techno as the foundation of his sound, also shaped by hardgroove and punk influences. This manifests as warmth, spaciousness, and intrigue in thoughtful narrative arcs.

Formosa

Formosa is a multidisciplinary Taiwanese-American DJ, artist, and designer who performs as "formosa" and as half of regular Pittsburgh queer party and music duo, Jellyfish. Behind the decks from Pittsburgh to New York, Toronto, London, Mexico, and Taipei, you can expect their sets to range from driving italo to electro, acid house, drum and bass, breakbeat, minimal, and more. Formosa will take you on a journey through driving bass lines and syncopated rhythms, sprinkled with playful melodies. You can catch their sets on SoundCloud, at any Jellyfish party, and at your local discotheque.

nonsite

nonsite is a local hardware techno producer.

Martingale

Bubbling and growling hypnotic and energetic techno.

events.title: The Summer Slow Down with Cass
events.description: The summer slow down is your invitation to take a big energetic exhale and pause before going into the next season. As we conclude one of the busiest times of year filled with picnics, parties and celebrations you’re invited to pause. In a culture, where constant striving is the norm the summer slow down is the antidote to busyness, burn out. This is an opportunity to refresh mental acuity and physically rest.  We will enter restorative yoga postures that transport you into a savasana state. The shapes are supported by props to create a gentle opening rather than deep stretching.

events.title: Papermaking Series with Katy DeMent
events.description: Learn to utilize tools, materials, and processes of making your own paper ! (photo credit: Nathan Shaulis) 6-Week Series Date: Tuesdays, September 29 – November 3, 2026 Time: 5:30pm-8:30pm Description: Katy will share her decades of experience and deep knoweldge of histories, fibers, tools, processes, and joys of papermaking. Throughout the series, you can expect a full and comprehensive introduction to processes of creating paper. This series will introduce you to how to use the Contemporary Craft’s hollander paper beater, a tool for turning fibers into pulp. You will also learn to work with dyed pulps, as well as create collages by adding elements directly into your paper before it dries. The series will cover the following topics (schedule is subject to change): Week 1 “101” Papermaking introduction and Western sheet forming Week 2 “Color” Pulp painting with colorful dyed pulps Week 3 “Texture” Adding texture and random inclusions Week 4 “Plants” Paper straight from plants! Week 5 “Collage” Handmade Paper: Wet on wet collage Week 6: “Wet Bound Books!” Handmade paper books Tuition: $270 + $40 materials fee Materials: All materials will be provided Registration: Register through Eventbrite. If you are viewing this listing on the Contemporary Craft website on your phone, please click this link to visit the Eventbrite registration page. Scholarships: We really want you to join us in the studio! Partial and full scholarships are available—with some limitations—to alleviate some of the financial burden of attending a class. Please fill out the scholarship application here! You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Senior Education Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1639. Location: Contemporary Craft, Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Papers Studio, which is on the first floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Paper Studio from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 8 stairs to attend One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. The Paper Studio is located down the hallway from this entrance. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call (and leave a message for) Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1639 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded through Eventbrite, or you may leave your workshop fee in your Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least 3 days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds can be given without 3-days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist ” For my entire life I have been a working artist, organic gardener, and beekeeper. I create handmade paper as a means to an end. Paper art works take the form of: art lighting, shadow box, stationary, books and sculptures all crafted from sustainably collected plants, recycled and invasive fibers. Each piece is a vignette that holds a visual narrative. Through layers of vintage ephemera, photos and bits of cloth, tales are told. When etched images are included the dialogue begins. Toys, natural and found objects punctuate the story. No material is arbitrary; I am influenced by overlooked materials found in my community, my own back yard. Rusty old tools are mashed together with deconstructed plants; this is where I find humor, combining these unlikely fellows. Often my works invite the viewer to playfully interact with the art work through light and kinetic elements that bring the imagery to life.” – Katy DeMent

events.title: World of Music: Las Áñez (Colombian Folk, Pop & Electronic Fusion)
events.description:
Prepare to be hypnotized by the musical stylings of sibling duo Las Áñez. The Áñez twins’ music is designed to be performed live with a loop pedal and small instruments, in a minimal yet enchanting concert style. Their shows include songs from their four award-winning albums, which have captivated audiences in ten countries across the Americas and Europe with their unique blend of folklore and the avant-garde. 
This program is presented as a part of Songs in the Key of She, a new concert series taking place in Chicago, New York, and Pittsburgh that features and celebrates women musicians and composers from around the world. Produced by the Chicago-based nonprofit Torito Arts in collaboration with City of Asylum, the series aims to combat the underrepresentation of female musicians in the male-dominated music industry. Songs in the Key of She is a platform in which talented women in music share their creativity and stories with new audiences. 

This engagement of Las Áñez is made possible in part through the Performing Arts Global Exchange program of Mid Atlantic Arts. 

About the Artist:

The Áñez sisters are Juanita and Valentina Añez Rothmann. Both sisters sing on all their songs, half of which are composed and arranged by each of them, and they are the producers of their first three albums. Juanita plays the cuatro and percussion, and Valentina is a pianist and percussionist. Their albums include Silbidos (2017), Al Aire (2017), Reflexión (2020), Paralelas (2023), and, most recently, Duálismo Magico (2026).

About Your Visit: 
The in-house restaurant, Cucina Alfabeto, is open for dinner from 5 to 10 p.m. Please visit OpenTable (https://www.opentable.com/r/alfabeto-pittsburgh) or call 412-435-1111 to make a reservation.

events.title: Jenny Owen Youngs and Northcote
events.description: Doors 7PM | Show 8PM $20 ADV | $25 DOSJenny Owens Young with her exceptional new Yep Roc debut, Avalanche, Youngs delivers a main course worthy of the wait. Written with a series of friends including S. Carey, Madi Diaz, The Antlers Peter Silberman, and Christian Lee Hutson and recorded with producer Josh Kaufman (Bonny Light Horseman, The Hold Steady, Cassandra Jenkins, Josh Ritter), the collection is an achingly beautiful exploration of loss, resilience, and growth from an artist whos experienced more than her fair share of each in recent years.Theres a good deal of heartbreak and disappointment in this music, Youngs explains, but it ultimately gives way to excitement and promise, to the incredible, immeasurable bliss of falling in love and finding yourself again. These songs travel the whole emotional spectrum.That kind of range has been Youngs calling card from the very start. Born and raised in rural New Jersey, she fell in love with The Beatles at an early age before eventually finding her way to The Cranberries and Elliott Smith in high school. Her self-recorded debut, Batten Down The Hatches, landed a high-profile sync in the Showtime series Weeds and led to a deal with Nettwerk Records, which re-released the album along with her 2009 follow-up, Transmitter Failure. Widespread acclaim and dates with the likes of Regina Spektor, Ingrid Michaelson, Frank Turner, and Aimee Mann followed, but by the time Youngs released her third album, 2012s An Unwavering Band Of Light, she was ready for a change of pace, moving to LA to focus on writing for other artists and for film and TV. In 2016, Youngs co-wrote Pitbulls Bad Man, which debuted at the 58th annual Grammy Awards; in 2017, she co-wrote Shungudzos Come On Back, which was featured in the Fifty Shades Freed soundtrack; and in 2018, she co-wrote Panic! At The Discos smash hit High Hopes, which went five-times platinum and broke the record for most weeks atop Billboards Hot Rock Songs chart. Along the way, Youngs also launched Buffering The Vampire Slayer, an episode-by-episode podcast devoted to Buffy The Vampire Slayer that attracted more than 160,000 monthly listeners and led to a book deal with St. Martins Press. Youngs recently launched a new series with her podcasting partner/ex-wife called The eX-Files and has a narrative fiction podcast due out next year, as well.Northcote brings a powerful, resonant acoustic performance rooted in honesty, grit, andemotional depth. His voice carries a rare warmth equal parts weathered and hopeful and his songs land with the weight of lived experience. Expect a set that feelspersonal, grounded, and deeply moving.

Their unmistakably singular sound is known for its monolithic force, inventive production, and deceptively nuanced arrangements. The Body has produced a wealth of groundbreaking collaborations and benchmark albums which have changed the perceptions and directions of heavy music.

Supporting is a can't-miss lineup of heavy hitters:

Ritual Mass, technical death metal quartet with a new record out on the great 20 Buck Spin

Alamoans, local hardcore punk darlings, back after a long hiatus.

... and Dilettante, the Pittsburgh heavy drone veteran playing tunes to open and drones throughout the evening.

events.title: PGX 2026 - Pittsburgh Gaming Expo
events.description:
Pittsburgh Gaming Expo (PGX) 2026 returns October 2–4, 2026, bringing together gaming, tabletop, and geek culture alongside an impressive lineup of musical guests.

Headlining the music programming is POWERGLOVE, the legendary metal band known for their heavy metal covers of video game and pop culture themes (powerglovemusic.bandcamp.com). Also featured is LORDS OF THE TRIDENT, a high-energy power metal band from Madison, WI known for epic performances and elaborate stage theatrics (lordsofthetrident.bandcamp.com).

ARCADIA brings their unique 'Mario Kart Jazz!' experience to the expo — a jazz ensemble performing video game music arrangements. Joining them is KATIE SHESKO on flute, adding a classical touch to the gaming music celebration.

The expo also features a special DUNGEON SYNTH LOUNGE showcasing:
- FOGLORD – atmospheric dungeon synth artist (foglord.bandcamp.com)
- HILLSFAR – dungeon synth project with a fantasy RPG aesthetic
- JENN TAIGA – dark/extreme dungeon synth

PGX is held annually in Pittsburgh, PA and celebrates all things gaming — video games, tabletop RPGs, board games, card games, and geek culture — combined with live music and entertainment.

events.title: Jaguar w/ Coffintexts
events.description:
Jaguar // feat. COFFINTEXTS & EPO (10/2)

Part Miami Bass, vintage house bounce, and tribal euphoria, Coffintexts’ music is a cocktail of indulgence
served straight from the queer underground.
When Coffintexts first burst onto the club scene in the late ‘10s, she was part of a new cohort of Miami
producers reshaping dance music. Equally influenced by everything from 90s tribal rhythms to Latin
American-inflected Club to UK rave, she emerged as part of the city’s new guard. Putting out records on
labels including Omnidisc, Club Romantico, Club QU, Classico, and a forthcoming record on TraTraTrax,
she has quickly established herself as one of the Magic City’s most vibrant musicians.

Even within this crowded field, Coffintexts acts as a unique center of gravity. While drawing from the
percussive promiscuity of her Peruvian heritage and the bass weight of her hometown, she also
gravitated towards the cerebral funk of ‘90s hardgroove, wiggly house, and the chromatic polish of UK
techno. Cutting her teeth in house parties and gay clubs across Miami, she’s always gravitated towards
the minimal, groove-focused energy of dance music at its most muscular and hypnotic. This background
has put her into conversation not just with the 305, but with the larger global queer dance music
cosmology.

There aren’t many producers and DJs who marry the paranoid and the psychedelic, the euphoric and the
illicit, the darkroom and the big room, the mind and the body, like Coffintexts.
As a producer, she’s just as comfortable turning out lean and stripped back techno as she is sultry,
bottom-heavy downtempo with occasional partner-in-crime Jonny from Space. Her DJing is just as
adventurous. Her mixes for outlets like Crack and Mixmag showcase an ambitious and daring style where
she jumps between tempos, eras, and genres without ever losing sight of that central current of hip-
swinging groove. It’s this intuitive and bodily approach to mixing that has kept dance floors from Miami to
Shanghai to Bristol, from Nowadays to III Points Festival to Razzmatazz gyrating and sweating it out until
the early hours.

Our dear friend EPO is back from Italy to get the crowd moving.

percussive promiscuity of her Peruvian heritage and the bass weight of her hometown, she also
gravitated towards the cerebral funk of ‘90s hardgroove, wiggly house, and the chromatic polish of UK
techno. Cutting her teeth in house parties and gay clubs across Miami, she’s always gravitated towards
the minimal, groove-focused energy of dance music at its most muscular and hypnotic. This background
has put her into conversation not just with the 305, but with the larger global queer dance music
cosmology.

There aren’t many producers and DJs who marry the paranoid and the psychedelic, the euphoric and the
illicit, the darkroom and the big room, the mind and the body, like Coffinte

events.title: Basketry: Cherokee-Style Twill Floor Basket with Traycee Bosle
events.description: Elevate your basketry skills in this 4-part series and create an impressive, functional work of art! Basketry: Cherokee-Style Twill Floor Basket with Traycee Bosle four-part series Date: Saturdays October 3, 10, 17, 24 Time: 10AM-1 PM Description: Designed for students with some basketweaving experience, this four-week workshop explores the art of twill basketry through the creation of a striking floor basket in an elegant urn shape. Over four three-hour sessions, participants will learn the fundamentals of twill construction, including how to build a twill base, execute a dramatic double-diamond twill pattern, and shape the basket into a graceful urn form. Emphasis will be placed on technique, structure, and pattern development. Students will leave with an impressive, functional basket—perfect to enjoy at home or present as a memorable handmade gift. Tuition: $210 + $40 materials fee Note: Full and partial tuition scholarships are often available—with some limitations—to offset some of the financial burden of attending a class. Find more information and the scholarship application here. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Senior Education Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Materials: All materials will be provided. Location: Contemporary Craft, Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Paper Studio, which is on the first floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Paper Studio from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 8 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. The Paper Studio is located down the hall from this entrance. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything that would be helpful for us to know before you arrive, please leave a message for Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or by email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist Traycee Bosle is a professional basket weaver at Craftisinal Creative Works—her arts studio in Pittsburgh, PA. She is a member of the Handweavers Guild of America and the Fiber Arts Guild of Pittsburgh. With over 1500 works in several different weaving styles under her belt, you can find her work in homes across the U.S. Basketweaving is an ancient art that crosses nearly all time, geographic, political, and social boundaries. It’s rooted in history, mathematics and pattern, color theory and design—with so much to offer—yet it’s nearly a lost art. Traycee has made it her mission to share her love for this once ubiquitous and critical skill with people of all ages. Her classes are fun, informative and personalized! She provides hands-on, individualized instruction using her own specially designed basket kits to teach the fundamentals of the art and meet each student where they are in their skill level. Whether you are an absolute beginner or have already made a few baskets, you will walk away with new skills and a beautiful basket you can use every day.

events.description: Learn the basics of woodturning by making your own wooden ballpoint pen! 3-Hour Workshop Date: Saturday, October 3rd, 2026 Time: 10am–1pm Description: In this beginning woodturning workshop, students will learn the foundations of woodturning to turn their own wooden pen! This class will explore the lathe, different methods of shaping wood on it, and shop safety. All materials, including the pen hardware, are provided. This is a great project to begin your woodturning journey! Each student will leave with their own wooden ballpoint pen—handmade on the lathe by them! events.title: Introduction to Weaving: Beginner Basics with Luca Budofsky
events.description: Weaving-curious? This workshop will introduce you to various types of looms, and will get you started weaving on a frame loom! Introduction to Weaving: Beginner Basics with Jamie Boyle 3-hour workshop Date: Saturday, October 3 Time: 2:00pm – 5:00pm Description: Curious about different kinds of looms? Want to try weaving but you are not sure where to start? Let this workshop be a beginning for you! Jamie will share some weaving basics and will guide you through weaving on a frame loom, which you will get to take home with you! Additionally, you will get to experience how some different types of looms function, including a rigid heddle loom and a multi-harness loom, guided by the general question: what does a loom do? In this class you will primarily work with your hands on a non-mechanical frame loom, but you will get an overview of various modes of weaving and get to try other looms in the studio! Tuition: $65 + $15 materials fee (if you are viewing this listing on your phone, scroll down to the bottom of the page for the class registration link) Materials: all materials are included. Registration: Register through Eventbrite! If you are viewing this listing via the Contemporary Craft website on your phone, please click this link to visit the Eventbrite registration page. Scholarships: We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are available—with some limitations—to alleviate some of the financial burden of attending a class. Scholarship application is found at this link . You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Fibers Program Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Location: Contemporary Craft, TImmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the Fibers Loft on the second floor. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. About the Artist Luca Budofsky is a multimedia artist from northern New Jersey. They hold a BFA from Carnegie Mellon University School of Art with a minor in Soft Technologies. They take particular interest in how textiles occupy shifting scales of material production and the way the woven structure breaks a surface into modular interlocking pieces. They love chance encounters with light casted on walls and sidewalks. They like noise. They think public radio is cool. They attribute their interest in cyclical events and repetitive processes to being a triplet. Luca has been recognized as an Andrew Carnegie Society Scholar and as a recipient of the Samuel Rosenberg Art Award. They work and weave in Pittsburgh, PA.

events.title: WITCHFEST
events.summary:
Follow us down a crooked road, winding and thorned. A voice of a forgotten one cries out, a siren song that echoes throughout eternity. As we make preparations for feasts of the dead yet to come, the Golden Thread OTO Lodge and Missrule Bookings conjoin to bring you Witchfest, a six-act experimental/noise show.
Joining our coven on this day will be the last gasps of a dying Foolosopher; Malleus in an orchestra of trumpet, microphone, digital delay and speakers; N3tizenfour's sonic square and compass; FLOOD in a practice of Oneness, in the style of amplifier worship; the pissy moany leaky groany creature electronics and grief rituals of Farrah Faucet; and a harmonium meditation by Mother Stellar Hagstone.
Come early for our opening ceremony. The way shall be made clear, and so will you. 
We hope to initiate you very soon.

Witchfest - October 3rd, 2026 - Doors 3PM. Show 4PM - $20
Golden Thread OTO - 300 Camp Horne Rd
Flyer by @divineclowncar

Please note that this is a SOBER space. We ask that this is respected.
The Golden Thread OTO Lodge is located 15 minutes north of Downtown Pittsburgh near Emsworth. The building which hosts the Lodge can be identified by its pizza mural on the front wall. Patrons are asked to park behind the building and to enter via the back door, up a flight of metal stairs. Parking in front is limited and should be reserved for people with mobility issues. events.title: Shapes: Jin & Juice, PVKVSV (Live), Gusto
events.description:
Three sides to a triangle - COLLAPSE, the Universal Observer, and YOU.

We’ve rotated our usual Shape for a special Saturday treat:

Devoted to the evolutionary essence of Black Dance Music, Jin & Juice @jinandjuic.e approaches the decks with curiosity, sensuality, and intention. Weaving club anthems through house and ghettotech with an intention that will hit every corner of our 4-point floor, she has brought her sound to spaces including Rinse France and the Carnegie Museum of Art. If you caught her 2023 Honcho Campout set at the Grove, you already know what’s coming.

PVKVSV [pah•kah’•sah] @pvkvsv offers a rare live set to the void. Co-running Pittsburgh Open Decks and curating Brewery Sessions at Jackworth’s Ginger Beer, PVKVSV is the kind of artist who’s spent years holding space for others to experiment. This night it’s his turn, and we have no idea what to expect.

Gusto’s @gusto.misc sound is shaped by the underground house and techno he was raised on, and the reggaeton and dembow that surrounded him growing up Dominican-American in the Bronx. A resident DJ and booker at Hot Mass who also runs DETOUR and MISC, Gusto carries those roots into Pittsburgh’s scene.

|𓁿||𓁿||𓁿||𓁿|
Tea & electrolytes will be freely provided. Join us and become one in ecstatic geometry.

Tix: collapsepgh.com

Flyer by @treebug222

events.title: Spinning 1 Series with Jasmine (Min) Davis
events.description: Learn how to use a drop spindle and a spinning wheel to create your own yarn for knitting, crocheting, weaving, and/or admiring!!! Spinning 1 Series with Jasmine (Min) Davis 6-Part Series Workshop! Date: Tuesdays, October 6 – November 17 (no class meeting on October 27) 6-9pm Description: Whether you dream of owning a flock of sheep someday or you want to join your local reenactors guilds—or anywhere in between!—spinning yarn is a skill that’s useful in a variety of situations. In this introductory class, students will learn how to use a drop spindle and a spinning wheel to create their own yarn for knitting, crocheting, weaving, and/or admiring. Over the course of six weeks, students will learn about two common tools for spinning yarn: drop spindles and spinning wheels. You’ll come away with two or more finished skeins of your own handspun yarn and the foundational skills you’ll need to continue building your spinning practice. PLEASE NOTE: Corriedale sheep wool is used for this class. If you have an allergy or prefer not to use animal fiber, please contact Senior Education Manager, Jamie Boyle by leaving a message at 412-465-1628 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org to discuss accommodations. Tuition: $270 + $30 materials fee Materials: Materials fee includes fiber and drop spindles. Students can use the spinning wheels in studio. Registration: Register via Eventbrite! If you are viewing this listing on the Contemporary Craft website on your phone, please click this link to visit the Eventbrite registration page. Scholarships: We really want you to join us in the studio! Partial and full tuition scholarships are available—with some limitations—to offset some of the financial burden of attending a class. Fill out the scholarship application here. You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions about scholarships, email Jamie Boyle at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Location: Contemporary Craft, TImmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the second floor. We strive to create a welcoming experience. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1639 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded through Eventbrite, or you may leave your workshop fee in your Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the artist: Jasmine Davis (Min) (she/her) is a fiber artist in Pittsburgh, PA . She enjoys spinning (yarn), spinning (poi), and spinning (in circles). She loves exploring color and texture across various textile mediums, and helping students discover possibilities within their materials.

events.title: Turning Night! Guided Open Studio with Matt Iannacci
events.description: Open to anyone who's tried their hand at woodturning, come spend the evening making your latest project under Matt's guidance! 3-Hour Guided Open Studio Date: Wednesday, October 7, 2026 Time: 6–9pm Description: Spend the evening on the lathes with fellow turners! Join us for Turning Night, a guided open studio session open to anyone who’s taken a woodturning workshop with us before—or anyone with experience on a wood lathe at all! Come with a project idea and Matt will guide you through the setup and technique to make it happen. This is the perfect opportunity for anyone with some turning experience to pursue their own project—but in the presence of an experienced woodturning instructor! The Studio has a small selection of turning blanks for sale, including pen blanks ( pen kit available here ), spindle blanks, and bowl blanks. However, for a more specific project, students are welcome to bring a wood blank of their own (we recommend Rockler if purchasing in advance). Join us for a night of woodturning community, guidance, and fun! Thanks to Turners Anonymous for the use of lathes during this workshop and Matt Iannacci for his expertise and enthusiasm! Tuition: $45 Materials: The Studio has a small selection of turning blanks for sale, or students can BYOB (blank)! Location: Contemporary Craft Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201) Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded by check, to your credit card, or Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. If you require accessibility accommodations, please let us know by calling 412.261.7003 and we are happy to assist you. About the Artist: Matt Iannacci “I have been woodturning for over 10 years, and doing wood flatwork for more than 7 years. I focus on medium-sized peices (vases, urns, etc., in woodturning, and jewelry boxes and frames in flatwork), usually seeking to combine different wood species to provide color and texture in my pieces. I am also the inventor of the JS3 jig, which is used to set up for compound-angle cuts necessary for splayed-stave woodturning, or boxes with leaning walls.” Outside of woodworking, Matt is a full-time mechanical engineer, a dad, and a saxophone and flute-player in a jazz band in the North Hills in Pittsburgh.

events.title: Nicky Diamonds
events.description: Doors 7PM | Show 8PM$15 ADV | $20 DOS21+Nicky Diamonds is an Afro-Indigenous Country-Roots/Blues Musician from San Antone, TX currently stationed in Nashville, TN. Pulling inspiration from old hymn books and family history, hes recounting the stories of his ancestors through his unique songwriting style. By keeping the roots of country and blues alive he puts a captivating twist to the tales and tunes of our people.Nicky spends most of his time touring the country with his 95 year old Dobro and occasionally with his band The Deepcuts. His new delta blues album, recorded at Willie Nelsons studio in Spicewood, Texas, is set to release in Spring 2025. If youre lucky enough youll catch Nicky at a Honky Tonk or Juke Joint close to home. His live show is a sight to see and youll leave with a groove stuck in your bones.

events.title: JAY JURDEN
events.description: Jay Jurden Jay Jurden is the star of the new Hulu comedy special Yes Ma’am, a breakout hour that solidifies him as one of the sharpest and most original comedic voices working today. Based in New York and originally from Mississippi, Jay has become a national standout thanks to his precise writing, magnetic presence, and a point of view that is both deeply personal and universally funny. The special is now available on all streaming platforms. Why'd We Book It? Watching Jay and Caleb on the So True podcast last year brought us to tears. events.title: The Unsolved Mystery of Ms Patsy Climbe
events.description:
Guess who is hitting the road?? The Nocturnal Creatures Troupe is going on tour, and you just might catch us creepin’ in a city near you!

Nocturnal Creatures Troupe presents: The Unsolved Mystery of Ms. Patsy Climb
An absurd puppet musical exploring the lives of three misfits on their quest to make it as street performers in the French Quarter of New Orleans. The Trio gets into all sorts of shenanigans, from getting addicted to “Crusties Hotdog Stand” , to refuting allegations of eating an ex lovers head. The story is narrated by Detective Bark, who uses his keen senses and logical mind to sniff out clues from the baffling events that have occurred. Will the creatures find fame? Or will struggles between the bandmates stop them from getting picked up by a label? Is their lead glockenspiel a blood thirsty diva? Will Detective Bark be able to crack this case wide open, and earn the title “GOOD BOY”? All these questions answered and more in The Nocturnal Creatures Show!!

We are so excited to be joined by our magical friend and skilled puppeteer Maya, @teethforbangs !!! YAY

events.title: Teddy Duchamp's Army Record Release Show
events.description:
Teddy DuChamp's Army have a new record in 2026!
"...the spirit never dies."
is being released on October 9th via legendary Philly punk label Creep Records and Sweet Cheetah in the US, Engineer Records in the UK and Scene police Records in Europe.

This records features J Robbins (JAWBOX, Burning Airlines, Government Issue) on bass.
Mario Quintero (Spotlights, Shiner, Molly Mcguire, Sisters) on 2nd guitar as well as the return of Mike Rock on guitar, Andy Wright on vox, and Jeff Kopanic on drums.
The album was produced and engineered by J Robbins at his Magpie Cage studio in Baltimore in January 2026 and mixed and mastered by Mario Quintero.
11 brand new songs! Punchy, melodic, with heavy, mellow and fast moments spread throughout classic TDA with a fresher feel.

Joining them will be Trace Remains - (ex Pikadori/Allies) Joey and Joel still being one of the best guitar duo's in Pittsburgh.

Latecomer - good old fast melodic punk in the vein of your favorite Lookout Records stuff

One If By Land - Fred and the boys have been doing it for years up in meadville/Franklin area with the Twirpentines and Signal Home. OIBL might be their best project to date, if you haven't seen them yet, get on it!

Show is Friday Oct.9th 6:30 doors at TECH 25 in Mt. Oliver only 2 blocks from 222 Ormsby and a short distance from Bottle Rocket. just two blocks off Brownsville road and on the busline.
112 St. Joseph St. Mt . Oliver 15210
ALL AGES and Alcohol with ID over 21 w/ donation. Beer donated by The Smiling Moose Brewery

There are multiple parking lots available around the building and street parking.

For those unfamiliar TECH 25 (run by Pete Spynda of Pandemic and Pittonkatonk) is an awesome noprofit that teaches classes on recording , live sound, lighting, rigging and many aspects of recording and live event production. We are stoked to help them shed some light on the space and their mission.
The Shiner show happened there last year and was awesome, we can't wait to have the show in this space.

events.title: Too Far Gone presents: Carré + Formosa
events.description:
We’re back.. This time around with a bass-laden soiree at SideQuest ( @sidequestpgh ), the basement space with a soundsystem rig well suited for the low-end freq’s, and two selectors who have long been on our radar:

@carre__carre
-
Carré is one of the leading figureheads in an international cohort of female, queer and non-binary producers pushing deep dubstep - alongside Too Far Gone favorites EMA, Darwin, Introspekt, Beatrice M and the Queer Steppa don, CCL - representing a refreshing shift in a genre that has long been heavily male-dominated, opening up a more inclusive space while also pushing a sound whose deep and meditative qualities speak to the dub part of dubstep.

UK dubstep’s lineage is the backbone of Carré’s sound where she balances a fine mix of sensual low-end rollers, percussive left-field techno, chrome-plated dubstep, and wonky drum workouts.

She has graced imprints like SPE:C, Bait, Woozy, and the formative dubstep imprint, Tempa ( @tempa.ltd ). Her latest string of EPs, Hibiscus + Citrine, highlight spacious rollers with US rap-meets-dubstep crossover - making it clear that she’s thoroughly comfortable weaving her own stew of influences into the modern bass music recipe.
With the dubstep baton finally passing to a new guard, Carré has cemented her role as one of its torchbearers.

@formosa.exe
-
Formosa (aka Steph Tsong) is a multi-disciplinary Taiwanese-American DJ, artist, designer and co-founder of Jellyfish ( @jellyfishpgh ),a long-running queer and trans-centered dance party based in Pittsburgh - known for its vibrant vibe curation, inclusive ethos, and a wide-range of eclectic sonic spectrums.

Outside from being one half of the city’s most in-demand party collective, Steph is a champion of the PGH dance underground - always willing to dot-connect, share knowledge or nerd out on her impeccable/extensive musical taste. Very lucky to have Formosa join us for opening duties where she will take us into the breakbeat-heavy depths of her sonic palette.

Advance tickets are available now via RA (with limited Early Bird pricing) - check link in bio

>>> artwork by none other than @jawnny5000

https://carre-carre.bandcamp.com/

events.description: Learn how to construct a hollow form pendant from metal clay! All-Day Workshop Date: Saturday, October 10, 2026 Time: 10am-5pm Description: Make a three-sided hollow pendant in silver metal clay! In the process, learn a versatile technique for constructing hollow pieces with multiple sides. For this introductory form, the front panel has volume, the back and top are flat, and the bail is a fun spiral. Students will complete one pendant up to the firing stage, and pieces will be fired later by the instructor. For those who work quickly, an in-class kiln firing will be offered. events.title: A Conversation with the Artist: Melissa English Campbell
events.description: Join us for a conversation with artist Melissa English Campbell as she shares her concept behind the works featured in Bodies in Motion. Join us for an engaging conversation with artist Melissa English Campbell as she shares the story, ideas, materials and processes behind her work. Through an informal interview and audience Q&A, gain deeper insight into the exhibition! Bodies in Motion (Currently on view through 10/31/2026) Bodies in Motion balances the strangeness of shifting realities with the familiarity and comfort of textiles. It is a partially immersive installation evoking proximity to textiles such as a warm towel or playing near blankets and sheets on a clothesline. The exhibition emerged when artist Melissa English Campbell recognized her tendency to mirror others’ accents, tone, and mannerisms as an unconscious survival strategy; a frequent adaptive response often shared by immigrants and their daughters. This experience is expressed through warp painted weavings presented in mirrored pairs. While images repeat, each work retains its own character, creating larger compositions that hold similarity and difference in productive tension. Panels are suspended throughout the gallery and on the walls, the textiles absorb sound and sway gently with air currents and passing bodies. Water recurs as a central motif, reflecting the fluid nature of identity and the body’s search for both challenge and comfort, as well as sanctuary from social expectations. Through repetition, comfort and strangeness, mirroring, and movement, Bodies in Motion invites viewers to consider identity not as fixed, but as something continuously shaped by adaptation, belonging, and change. Melissa English Campbell (b. 1969, San Francisco) holds a B.S. in Environmental Design from the University of California, Davis, and an MFA in Studio Arts from Kent State University. Her artwork has been exhibited globally, including at the Royal Albert Museum in the UK, Seoul, South Korea; Como, Italy; and New South Wales, Australia. Nationally, Melissa’s work has been shown at galleries such as San Jose Museum of Textiles, Columbus Museum of Craft, New Bedford Art Museum, Museum of Texas Tech University; Petaluma Center for the Arts, Hand Weaving Museum, and Contemporary Craft. She is a recipient of the Award of Excellence from the Ohio Council for the Arts. Recent artist residencies include The Chautauqua Institutes Artist Residency, Vermont Studio Center, Praxis TC2 Residency, and Berea College Artist Residency. Campbell currently lives and works in Northeast Ohio. Photo: Feet in Fawn Lake (detail), Courtesy of the Artist

events.title: Ultraviolet w/ Convextion, E.R.P., Shawn Rudiman, Paul Fleetwood
events.description:
Ultraviolet, a night of techno and electro featuring live performances from Convextion aka E.R.P. traveling from Dallas, TX, and Pittsburgh's own Shawn Rudiman, with resident DJ Paul Fleetwood rounding out the night.

Convextion is the alias of Gerard Hanson, a Dallas-based electronic musician known for deep, atmospheric techno and electro. He also records as E.R.P. (Electro Resistance Project), producing classic electro sounds with a futuristic edge. His Bandcamp can be found at convextion.bandcamp.com.

Shawn Rudiman is a Pittsburgh techno legend, a pioneer of the local scene known for his hardware-driven live sets blending techno, electro, and experimental sounds. His Bandcamp is at shawnrudiman.bandcamp.com.

Paul Fleetwood is a Ultraviolet resident DJ holding down the local electro and techno sound, as well as the force behind the Perimeter Junk label.

https://soundcloud.com/resident-advisor/ra265-convextion

https://soundcloud.com/neptunianinfluence/ni62-shawn-rudiman

events.title: Natural Dyeing: Eco-Printing with Fall Leaves w/ Kelly Lane
events.description: Create Wearable Art from Nature in this beginner-friendly natural-dyeing workshop! 3-Hour Workshop Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Time: 2pm-5pm Description: Join us in the Beth Wainwright Dye Lab at Contemporary Craft for a morning of learning with Kelly Lane, who will guide participants through the process of eco-printing, a method of transferring the shapes and marks of leaves and flowers onto fabric. And, create a uniquely printed, organic cotton bandana! In this workshop, we will capture the autumnal season by exploring the art of eco-printing, where the natural shapes of leaves and flowers are permanently transferred onto fabric through a process of bundling and steaming. We will cover various eco-printing techniques, focusing on a method that combines tannin-soaked fabric and an iron blanket to create rich, moody greys and the negative shapes of leaves. Tannins and iron are materials used to help the printing process. In the workshop, we will also talk more about these materials and where you might acquire them for future at-home printing. You can expect to learn how to prepare fabric and use a special technique to achieve clear, crisp prints. Your one-of-a-kind design will be created on an 18”, organic cotton bandana – the perfect accessory to enliven your fall wardrobe, or to give as a gift during the holiday season. At the end of the workshop, you will be given a project packet that includes details about the eco-printing process along with resources for repeating this method at home. All materials will be provided, but if you would like to bring your own leaves or other plant matter, please feel free to do so. This workshop is open to all skill levels – no prior experience is needed! Tuition: $65 + $15 materials fee Registration: Register through Eventbrite! If you are viewing this listing via the Contemporary Craft website on your phone, please click this link to visit the Eventbrite registration page. Scholarships: Note: We really want you to join us in the studio! Partial and full tuition scholarships are available—with some limitations—to offset some of the financial burden of attending a class. Scholarship application can be found here! You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Senior Education Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Materials: All materials will be provided. Location: Contemporary Craft, Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the second floor. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1639 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded through Eventbrite, or you may leave your workshop fee in your Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist Kelly is a natural dye and mixed media artist and educator. Her work is inspired by our innate connection to the natural world and the wellspring of wisdom that surfaces when we slow down and tune in to our surroundings. As an artist, she taps into this connection to create work that is an intermingled reflection of landscapes within and without. For each project, Kelly thoughtfully forages plants to create botanical palettes that imbue both formal beauty and conceptual depth. In addition to plant-based dyes, she also incorporates sustainable or rescued textiles in her work. With over 15 years of experience as a sustainable clothing designer, Kelly has a deep appreciation for natural fibers and the warmth they radiate. In addition to her artistic practice, Kelly loves sharing her passion for creating color with plants through teaching natural dye and ink-making workshops.

events.title: In Dead by Ten: Heaven & Hell
events.description:
Arise! It’s time for the third-annual In Dead by Ten Halloween Dance Party, presented by Hidden Harbor, THIS IS RED, and In Bed by Ten, returning on Saturday, October 17 to the stunning, century-old former Slovakian Catholic church that serves as THIS IS RED’s home base and event space in Munhall. Tickets are on sale NOW!

This year’s edition takes on a Heaven & Hell theme, with two levels of DJ’s offering two different dance experiences. Upstairs in the main hall “Pop Heaven,” Slim tha DJ and DJ MB will take you higher, while downstairs in the Disco Dungeon, DJ’s EZ Lou, Buscrates, and Formosa will light a fire under your feet.

Pay a visit to the Tarot Grotto with Tenorina for a frightfully good reading. And don’t forget the costume contest, now with a dance line at 9 p.m. to show off your moves with prizes for Best Group Costume, Best Presentation, and Most Creative. Be an angel, a devil, or both!

Throughout the multiple levels of the space, enjoy diabolically good tropical cocktails, beer, and wine from Hidden Harbor, Independent Brewing Company, Lorelei, and Golden Age, with eats by GA.

All past versions of this event have sold out ahead of the event date, so gather your crew and get your tickets now, with early-bird pricing now thru September 18. And special thanks to @rojowashere for concept and brainstorming!

events.title: Kara Frazier, Emily Lehr & the Foxglove Fellows, and Van Gilder
events.description: Doors 6PM | Show 7PM$10 ADV | $15 DOS21+ Kara Frazier: Nashville-based singer-songwriter Kara Frazier is a rare artist who inhabits the space between eras. Originally from Jacksonville, FL, she has spent over a decade honing a sound that blends bluesy vocals with southern roots and a pop-soul feel. Emily Lehr & the Foxglove Fellows: A native West Virginian, Emily Lehr finds inspiration in the Appalachian traditions of communal music-making and raw lyricism. From cozy solo performances in the living room to lively shows with her band, the Foxglove Fellows, Emily connects with live audiences to bring her stories to life with friends old and new. Van Gilder: Van Gilder is a should and r&b inspired rock band based in Pittsburgh, PA. Founded in 2016 by longtime friends and collaborators Adelaide Estep and Connor Bragg, the band quickly found their sound by blending different influences to cultivate something unique.

events.title: BECHDEL CAST TEN YEAR “Whoops We Didn’t Dismantle the Patriarchy” ANNIVERSARY TOUR
events.description: It’s been ten years, and we can still remember the fresh podcast. The recording equipment had never been used. The movies had never been watched. The Bechdel Cast was called “The Show of Dreams”… and it was, it really was! Join hosts Jamie Loftus and Caitlin Durante for a LIVE SHOW celebrating their TEN YEAR ANNIVERSARY of hosting The Bechdel Cast! Caitlin and Jamie are taking a look at the past decade of (genius, brilliant, important) discussions about film, and pondering how releasing radical mp3s every week didn’t fix global misogyny?! It will be a spectacular, full of videos, games, fan fic, Shrek references (Shreferences), you name it! It’s Halloween season, so come dressed as a movie character, because you bet your ass Jamie and Caitlin will be in costume! SEE YOU THERE!!!

events.title: Othello of the End Zone, or The Steel City Tragedy
events.description:
Step onto the 50-yard line for the New Hazlett’s first-ever co-production with DEMASKUS Theater Collective: Othello of the End Zone, or The Steel City Tragedy. Written by Franky D. Gonzalez, directed by Shaunda Miles McDill, and starring Cynthia Dallas and Michael Patrick Trimm, this high-stakes modern reimagining brings Shakespeare to the Northside stage. When Imani Othello is named Head Coach of America's most beloved football franchise, the pressure mounts on and off the field. This hard-hitting adaptation centers a Black woman calling the plays at the height of her power, confronting ambition, betrayal, and relentless doubt.
•	Dates: October 22–24 at 7:30 PM | October 24 at 2:00 PM | October 25 at 3:00 PM
•	Tickets: $50 (Thursday, Oct. 22: Pay-What-You-Can starting at $20)
•	Purchase: https://ci.ovationtix.com/36406/production/1291006
