events.title: Joomchi Paper with Rae Gold
events.description: Learn the ancient art of Joomchi, making laminated sheets of mulberry paper into a new sheet of paper. Date: Saturday, December 12, 2026 Time: 10am-1pm Description: We will learn the ancient art of making laminated sheets of mulberry paper into a new sheet of paper that can be used as is or can be part of collage, mixed media, or three dimensional work. Students will leave with a completed piece. Tuition: $65 + $25 materials fee We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are available to alleviate some of the financial burden of attending a class. Please fill out the application here! You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Fibers Program Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Materials: All materials will be provided. Location: Contemporary Craft, Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Papers Studio, which is on the first floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Paper Studio from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 8 stairs to attend One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. The Paper Studio is located down the hallway from this entrance. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call (and leave a message for) Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded through Eventbrite, or you may leave your workshop fee in your Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist Rae Gold has a BFA from Carnegie Institute of Technology (now Carnegie Mellon University). She created one of a kin wearables for 30 years, showing and selling at ACC Baltimore Craft Show, Philadelphia Museuem of Art Craft Show, Smithsonian Craft Show, and Washington Craft Show, among others. For the last ten years she has been creating three dimensional wet felted sculptures, two and three dimensional Joomchi work, and now playing with natural basketry forms.

events.title: Weave Your Own Towel with the CC Weave Coaches: Holiday Special!
events.description: Throw a shuttle like the Weave-a-Thon pros! Drop on in and weave a towel! We did the set up for you! Yes, absolute beginners welcome! DROP IN STYLE: 3-hour session! Date: Saturday, December 12! Time: Start times vary: 10 AM, 12PM, 2PM (and expect to stay for about 3 hours after your start time for your towel to reach completion!). You will select your start time when you register. Description: Weaving Curious? This is your chance!!! Absolute beginner drop-in style weaving has arrived! Throw a shuttle like the Weave-a-Thon pros! You, too, can make your very own towel! Come on in and weave on pre-dressed looms! Our team of Weave Coaches will prepare your looms before you get here! All, you will need to do is choose some yarn colors and throw a shuttle. And…..not to worry! our Weave Coaches will guide you through the process, offering tips for throwing those shuttles back and forth to build a special and custom towel of your very own design. What’s more, we will help you take the weaving off of the loom and finish and hem your towel before you leave the studio! You can expect your towel to be about 16 x 20 inches (and it will shrink after washing to about 14 x 18), so as a dear weaver once said these will be “towel-ish” sized, and all a bit different. A sweet hand towel to gift to a loved one or to brighten up your own room! This is a completely beginners welcome offering. No experience expected. There are different beginning time slots to choose. Plan to spend about 3 hours from your chosen start time. For this special holiday edition: Five weavers will be able to begin at each starting time; call up all of your best pals and have a SUPER FUN time together! This is offering is part of our Gift Guide suite of workshops, in which you get to learn something and make a gift for someone special at the same time! Tuition: $75 (materials included) Materials: All materials will be provided Registration: register through Eventbrite! If you are viewing this listing via the Contemporary Craft website on your phone, please visit this link which will take you to the Eventbrite listing. Scholarships: We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are available to offset some of the financial burden of attending a class. Please fill out the application here! You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Senior Edcuation Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Location: Contemporary Craft, Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the second floor. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded by check, to your credit card, or Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. Check out these weavers with their towels from past Weave Your Own Towel events !

events.title: Magnolia Boulevard w/ Madison Hughes
events.description: Doors 7PM | Show 8PM$15 ADV | $20 DOS21+With a southern rock tinged flavor of soulful americana, and a powerful female vocalist reminiscent of Tedeschi Trucks Band, Magnolia Boulevard has blossomed through devastation since forming in 2017. They pushed through the turmoil of COVID-19 that devastated the music industry, the sorrow following the death of their beloved drummer, and the joys of welcoming Maggies daughter into the world. Much like the band members of Magnolia Boulevard have endured the highs and lows of the past few years, so has their music. The bands emphatic and empowering anthems of love, self-discovery, grief, and uncertainty serve as a lesson to us all about lifes unpredictable nature and how to better live in the moment so we can appreciate everything and everyone around us before theyre gone.If patience is a virtue, then the current state of Magnolia Boulevard plays right into the long-held notion that sonic grandeur evolves in its own time and place one where the Lexington, Kentucky, rock-n-soul act is aiming to break into a national audience ready and roaring for the quintets soaring talents.Formed in 2017 by Noelle and Allen, the band came together when other creative endeavors werent fulfilling the artistic desires and professional expectations of what the duo were envisioning. It was time to push down the gas pedal on the possibility and potential of what Magnolia Boulevard could be, and ultimately has become in sonic design and in the live realm.The sound has been described as Appalachian Soul, and I really like that because of our Appalachian roots, Noelle says. You get a taste of folk with the songwriting portion, but you also have that rock and soul foundation. Madison Hughes will make you feel like someone finally said the thing out loud. Not loudly. She doesnt need to be. Her voice carries the kind of weight that sneaks up on you, warm and unhurried, until a single line stops you mid-drive and you sit in the parking lot a little longer than you planned.She grew up in Ponte Vedra Beach, Florida, idyllic by every measure, rooted in the same coastal Southern soil that gave the world Lynyrd Skynyrd, Tom Petty, the Allman Brothers, Tedeschi Trucks Band, and Ray Charles. Music was in the air before it was ever a choice. Her fathers folk-rock records: Springsteen, Jackson Browne, Bonnie Raitt, Sheryl Crow, Gillian Welch. Her mothers soft devastation: Dido, Sarah McLachlan, the Cranberries, Norah Jones. The grit and the tenderness both took root.She started writing songs in high school because heartbreak cracked her open and she couldnt say the hard things any other way. That instinct never left. Her sound refuses to sit still, grunge-folk grit threaded through country soul, blues-pop hooks bleeding into indie Americana, all of it held together by feel rather than formula. In high school she was the girl who sat with everyone at lunch, allergic to the idea that you had to pick a side. Thats still who she is. The genre-crossing isnt a strategy. Its just her nature.

events.title: Weave Your Own Towel with the CC Weave Coaches: Holiday Special!
events.description: Throw a shuttle like the Weave-a-Thon pros! Drop on in and weave a towel! We did the set up for you! Yes, absolute beginners welcome! DROP IN STYLE: 3-hour session! Date: Saturday, December 19! Time: Start times vary: 10 AM, 12PM, 2PM (and expect to stay for about 3 hours after your start time for your towel to reach completion!). You will select your start time when you register. Description: Weaving Curious? This is your chance!!! Absolute beginner drop-in style weaving has arrived! Throw a shuttle like the Weave-a-Thon pros! You, too, can make your very own towel! Come on in and weave on pre-dressed looms! Our team of Weave Coaches will prepare your looms before you get here! All, you will need to do is choose some yarn colors and throw a shuttle. And…..not to worry! our Weave Coaches will guide you through the process, offering tips for throwing those shuttles back and forth to build a special and custom towel of your very own design. What’s more, we will help you take the weaving off of the loom and finish and hem your towel before you leave the studio! You can expect your towel to be about 16 x 20 inches (and it will shrink after washing to about 14 x 18), so as a dear weaver once said these will be “towel-ish” sized, and all a bit different. A sweet hand towel to gift to a loved one or to brighten up your own room! This is a completely beginners welcome offering. No experience expected. There are different beginning time slots to choose. Plan to spend about 3 hours from your chosen start time. For this special holiday edition: Five weavers will be able to begin at each starting time; call up all of your best pals and have a SUPER FUN time together! This is offering is part of our Gift Guide suite of workshops, in which you get to learn something and make a gift for someone special at the same time! Tuition: $75 (materials included) Materials: All materials will be provided Registration: register through Eventbrite! If you are viewing this listing via the Contemporary Craft website on your phone, please visit this link which will take you to the Eventbrite listing. Scholarships: We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are available to offset some of the financial burden of attending a class. Please fill out the application here! You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Senior Edcuation Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Location: Contemporary Craft, Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the second floor. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1628 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded by check, to your credit card, or Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. Check out these weavers with their towels from past Weave Your Own Towel events !

events.title: STEELERS GAME (vs Ravens)
events.description: STILLERS SUNDAY at Bottlerocket This season, there's no better place to watch our beloved Steelers than your neighborhood Bottlerocket! With non-annoying music during the commercial breaks, $3 Draft Beers, Steelers Bingo, and food from our brand new BottleDogs cart - every Sunday it's the best dive bar in town, and that means the best place to watch a ballgame. The bar is open to ALL AGES & totally free! Come hang! STEELERS BINGO We give you a sheet of things that will proably happen at some point during a Steelers game (Aaron Rogers first down point, Mike Mccarthy hometown mention, TJ Watt Sacks, someone in the bar disagreeing with a coaching decision, etc.) - you mark them off as they happen, and win! Even if the Steelers lose you can still go home a winner from the prize pile - and we don't interrupt a second of the game to play, so if you're locked in to the actual game, have no fear.

events.title: Needle Felting: Bird of the Month: Red Breasted Nuthatch with Erin Carlson
events.description: January (2027)’s bird of the month: Red Breasted Nuthatchl! Learn to needle felt, while enjoying a detailed look at this fascinating bird! 3-hour workshop Date: Thursday, January 7, 2027 Time: 6pm-9pm Description: Learn to needle felt or sharpen your skills while creating your own Red Breasted Nuthatch . Fiber artist and backyard bird enthusiast Erin Carlson of Red Cottage Fiber Studio will guide you through the needle felting process as you look closely to observe the shape and markings of the species and gain a deeper appreciation of our avian neighbors. Adventurous beginners welcome. Please note that we will be using sharp needles and repetitive, detailed hand motions. About the 2026-27 Bird of the Month Needle Felting Series : Due to popular demand, Contemporary Craft is thrilled to once again partner with instructor Erin Carlson to offer this series of workshops! While first offered virtually during the pandemic, this year will be live and in-person! Classes will occur the first Thursday of each month from 6-9pm and run from March 2026-February 2027. Join us for as many classes as you like. Choose your favorite bird or join us for all 12 to complete your very own flock. The bird selections are as follows: March: American Robin April: Scarlet Tanager May: Barn Swallow June: Eastern Bluebird July: Ruby-Throated Hummingbird August: American Goldfinch September: Downy Woodpecker October: Barn Owl November: Chickadee December: Northern Cardinal January(2027): Red Breasted Nuthatch February(2027): Red Winged Blackbird Tuition: $65 + $10 materials fee (per workshop) (if you are viewing this listing on your phone, scroll down to the bottom of the page for the class registration link) Materials: all materials are included. events.title: Weekend 101: Introduction to Weaving on a Floor Loom with Jamie Boyle
events.description: In this weekend beginner workshop, go from a pile of yarn to woven cloth, learn how to use a floor loom, and make new friends! Weeklong Intensive: Introduction to Weaving Date: Saturday January 16 and Sunday January 17, 2027 Time: 10am – 5pm (both days!) Description: Let’s dive deep into weaving for a weekend! This is a 100% beginner weaving workshop, where we will learn to use multi-harness floor looms to create cloth! We will work with 8-harness looms, and explore myriad ways of creating interlacements of warp and weft to create cloth! Because of the “intensive” format of this workshop, we will be able to immerse oursleves completely in the fun and magic of weaving and using a loom. You can expect to learn how to go from having bunch of cones or balls of yarn to woven cloth! We will go through steps and ways to dress the loom (that means get the yarn on the loom) and we will try different techniques for interlacing yarn! Our goal will be a woven sampler of possibilities and a foundation for future weaving work! You will also have access to your loom and open studio for one week after the class to practice what you learned! Tuition: $220 + $30 materials fee Materials: All materials will be provided Registration: Register via Eventbrite! If you are viewing this listing via the Contemporary Craft website on your phone, please click this link to visit the Eventbrite registration page. Scholarships: : We really want you to join us in the studio! Full and partial tuition scholarships are available to offset some of the financial burden of attending a class. Please fill out the application here! You can expect to hear from someone on the CC staff within 2 weeks. If you have any questions, email Jamie Boyle, Fibers Program Manager, at jboyle@contemporarycraft.org, or leave a voice message for them at 412-465-1628. Location: Contemporary Craft, Timmons Studios (5688 Butler St., Pittsburgh, PA 15201). Note, this workshop will take place in the Fleischner Family Fibers Loft, which is on the second floor of the building. There are 2 entrances to the Timmons Studios. • One entrance is facing Butler Street. To access the Fibers Loft from the Butler Street facing entrance, there are a total of 32 stairs to ascend. • One entrance is facing 57th Street. This entrance is accessible by ramp, with no stairs to ascend. There is a lift inside the building to access the second floor. If there are accessibility accommodations we can provide, or if there is anything you would like us to know before you arrive, please feel free to call Jamie Boyle at 412-465-1639 or email jboyle@contemporarycraft.org. Cancellations and Refunds: Workshop cancellations are decided three business days before the start date. If workshops must be cancelled due to insufficient enrollment, the entire class fee will be refunded by check, to your credit card, or Contemporary Craft account for future workshops. Refund Policy: Student refund requests must be made at least three business days before a class begins. There will be a $25 cancellation fee. No refunds will be given without three-business days notice. Processing of refunds takes approximately three weeks. About the Artist Jamie Boyle is an artist and weaving teacher who recently moved back to Pittsburgh after living for more than a decade in a studio apartment in Brooklyn, NY with a partner and two cats. They attended public school from grade school through graduate school. Jamie’s first weaving teacher was the artist Ann Hamilton, in whose studio they worked for several years after completing an MFA in sculpture. Subsequently, Owyn Marisol Ruck, Kira Silver, Isa Rodrigues, Kelly Valetta, and Jose Picayo taught Jamie who to use a multi-harness floor loom as a tool for weaving. They have had the great honor of sharing a love of weaving with communities of learners at the Park slope Center for Successful Aging, the National Council of Jewish Women NY Lifetime Learning Center, the Museum of Arts and Design, and the Textile Arts Center, among others. Jamie has participated in artist residencies at the Textile Arts Center (Brooklyn, NY); the Museum of Arts and Design (New York, NY); through the SU-CASA program administered by the Brooklyn Arts Council; and Contemporary Craft (Pittsburgh, PA). Currently, they serve as the Fibers Program Manager at Contemporary Craft.

events.title: MARK NORMAND (Thursday, Early)
events.description: Dubbed by Jerry Seinfeld as the “best young up and coming comic,” Mark Normand is quickly becoming one of the most talked about touring comedians on the scene. Normand’s NEW one- hour Netflix special, SOUP TO NUTS, has been a staple in the streamers’ Top Ten since its July 25th premiere. This follows Normand’s self-released special, 2020’s “Out to Lunch” which amassed over 12 million views on YouTube. He also starred on Netflix’s Season 3 of The Stand Ups. Why'd We Book It? Excited to have the witty Mark Normand joining us this August. Mark is known for his fast talking mixed with puns, one-liners, and quick punchlines which is why we like him. He is quick and to the point, but still keeps a high quality. From podcasts to late night appearances Mark has been in the comedy world for years and has the receipts to back it up. For Fans Of... Gary Gulman, Sam Morrill, Nate Bargatze Extended Bio: An extremely prolific stand-up, he previously had a one-hour and a half hour Comedy Central special and has made an unparalleled seven appearances on “Conan,” four appearances on “The Tonight Show with Jimmy Fallon,” and has also appeared on “The Late Show with Stephen Colbert.” Mark IS A FREQUENT GUEST ON “The Joe Rogan Experience,” AND HOSTS his own podcasts “Tuesdays with Stories” and “We Might Be Drunk." Seating/Show Information: Limit 4 tickets per transaction. This show will have theater seating. Seats will be assigned upon arrival, or can be chosen ahead of time for an additional fee. QR Code Ordering will be available for this performance. Doors open at 5pm. Don't miss our famous Bottlerocket Pre-Show Clip Collection, beginning one hour before the start of the performance. This show is ALL AGES *all information subject to change as needed. Bottlerocket FAQ: All shows starting before 10pm are all ages unless otherwise noted. Free parking is available at 824 Industry Street and 205 Allen Street, as well as other public lots in the area. Live Music shows have limited seating options, please arrive early or reach out to the venue directly if you know that you require a seat. Doors open at 5pm for all shows unless noted otherwise. The time listed on the ticket is the event's true start time. Most shows have a preshow experience starting 1 hour before the show. Our full refund policy can be viewed here Please contact us ahead of time with any accesibilty requests or concerns, we're happy to accomodate you. More FAQ's can be found here

For Premium Seating and Suites information please email peterseneventscenter@pitt.edu or call 412-648-3054
